title: Jibril — the Trustworthy Spirit
subtitle: The angel who carried every word of the final revelation
sources: Qur'an 2:97 — 'he brings down the revelation upon your heart'
Qur'an 26:193-194 — 'the trustworthy spirit has descended with it'
Sahih Muslim 8 — the hadith of Jibril in human form
Qur'an 96:1 — the night of Hira

chapters.heading: Iqra
chapters.body: He came to a man in a cave and said one word that rebuilt the world: Iqra — Read (96:1). The Qur'an names him Ruh al-Amin, the Trustworthy Spirit, and says of the revelation: 'the trustworthy spirit has descended with it upon your heart, that you may be of the warners' (26:193-194). He came in his true form only twice to the Prophet ﷺ — at the cave of Hira, and at the Ajyad pass in Makkah, when the Prophet ﷺ saw him filling the horizon with six hundred wings, having blocked out the sky (Bukhari 349). And he came disguised as a man in spotless clothes, with dark hair, sitting among the companions, resting his hands on his thighs — to ask about Islam, iman, and ihsan, so the Prophet ﷺ could teach the religion through his questions (Muslim 8). The greatest teacher in the ummah's history is an angel who asked the right questions. Every word of the Qur'an, every verse recited tonight anywhere on earth, traveled to humanity through him.

familyQuestion: Jibril asked questions so the companions could learn. What question could you ask tonight that would teach your whole family?

title: Mika'il — the Angel of Provision
subtitle: The one by whose hand the rain falls and the crops rise
sources: Qur'an 2:98 — named with Jibril as an angel of Allah
Sunan al-Tirmidhi 3367 — the hadith of his laughter over a man's mercy

chapters.heading: The Laughter Over a Debt Forgiven
chapters.body: Mika'il is named in the Qur'an beside Jibril (2:98), and his charge is the provision of the worlds: the rain that falls, the seeds that split, the harvest that feeds a planet. The tradition gives him a face the heart can hold: a hadith tells of a man who pulled his camel's head away from the fodder of others' fields, and that night Allah sent him a dream — or a vision — of Mika'il laughing, and the news came back to the Prophet ﷺ, who explained: your Lord laughs at the man who, able to wrong his brother, refrains — and Mika'il laughs with Him (Tirmidhi 3367, hasan). The angel of provision laughing over a forgiven debt: sustenance itself rejoices when mercy beats greed. Provision, the story teaches, is not only sent down from the sky; it is released by what the hand refuses to take.

familyQuestion: Provision itself rejoiced over one act of mercy. What is your hand holding that it should release this week?

title: Israfil — the Trumpet
subtitle: The horn is raised to his lips; the wait itself is mercy
sources: Qur'an 39:68 — 'the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead'
Muslim 2940 — the hadith naming Israfil and the stillness before the command

chapters.heading: The Longest Silence in Creation
chapters.body: The hadith names him: Israfil, the one with the Trumpet, and describes the waiting — his eyes turned toward the Throne, awaiting a command that has not yet come (Muslim 2940). Think about what the wait means. The Day has been prepared, the books have been bound, the graves have been filled for millennia — and still the blast has not sounded, because the matter that must happen first is the last person who will ever repent. The Qur'an describes the moment itself: 'the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills; then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on' (39:68). Twice: once to end, once to begin. Every day that passes without the blast is a day the mercy of waiting is still extended to you — the Qur'an calls the time between the two blows a period when the people wait in the graves as in a sleep, and the earth will shine with the light of its Lord (39:69). The scariest sound in existence is still being delayed for your sake.

familyQuestion: Israfil's blast is delayed so you can repent. If today were the last day of the delay, what would you fix tonight?

title: Malak al-Mawt — the Angel of Death
subtitle: 'He has been entrusted with you' — and his door is always open
sources: Qur'an 32:11 — 'say: the angel of death, who has been entrusted with you, will take you'
Muslim 2878 — the believer's soul taken 'as a drop slips from a waterskin'

chapters.heading: The Gentle Taking
chapters.body: The Qur'an answers the question no one can escape: 'Say: the angel of death, who has been entrusted with you, will take you; then to your Lord you will be returned' (32:11). Entrusted with you: the taking of your soul is a trust, performed with the care of a duty owed to Allah — not a theft. And the hadith shows the gentleness of the trust: when the soul of the believer is taken, it comes out as a drop slips from a waterskin — smooth, clean, without tearing — and the angels receive it with the words: peace be upon you; enter Paradise for what you used to do (Muslim 2878). The same angel comes to the tyrant, and the taking is everything the first was not. Same door, two weathers — the difference is not the angel; it is the soul he is asked to carry. In the whole library of the Unseen, no card makes the afterlife nearer than this one.

familyQuestion: The Qur'an calls death a 'return' and a 'trust.' What would you want the record of your trust to say when it is handed over?

title: The Scribes on Your Shoulders
subtitle: Noble recorders, knowing whatever you do — writing right now
sources: Qur'an 82:10-12 — 'noble recorders, knowing whatever you do'
Qur'an 50:17-18 — 'when the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left'

chapters.heading: The Two Receivers
chapters.body: 'Man does not utter any word except that with him is an observer prepared' (50:18). The Qur'an gives them their posts: two angels, one on the right shoulder recording the good, one on the left recording the evil — and when a servant intends a bad deed, the recorder on the left is ordered to wait: if the deed is done, write it; if the intention passes and the deed is abandoned, Allah commands it not to be written at all (Muslim 131). Read that again: the angels hold their pens for your hesitation. The record begins with action, and mercy writes over intention. At the end, the book is presented: 'Read your book; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant' (17:14). The most quietly motivating sentence in the app: nothing you have ever done is missing from the record — and nothing you almost did is held against you.

familyQuestion: The pen waits during your hesitation. What deed are you hesitating on right now — good or bad?

title: Munkar & Nakir — the Two Questioners
subtitle: The three questions of the grave — told to prepare, never to terrorize
sources: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1071 — the three questions, graded sahih
Qur'an 14:27 — 'Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter'

chapters.heading: Man Rabbuka?
chapters.body: When the believer is placed in the grave, the hadith teaches, two angels come to him and ask three questions: Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is this man who was sent among you? (Tirmidhi 1071). The servant who answered honestly in life answers in the grave: My Lord is Allah; my religion is Islam; that is the Messenger of Allah — and a caller from the heavens confirms: My servant has spoken truth. Then the grave is widened as far as the eye can see, and a door to Paradise is opened to him, and he sleeps in the garden of the barzakh until the Trumpet. The design rule this library keeps: the grave is told to prepare, never to terrorize — the card ends where the Qur'an ends, at the firm word that holds a person steady: 'Allah keeps firm those who believe, with the firm word, in worldly life and in the Hereafter' (14:27). The answers are learned in the living room, not in the grave.

familyQuestion: The three questions are about knowing, not performance. Could you answer all three tonight, out loud, in one sentence each?

title: The Angels You Never See
subtitle: The qarin, the dhikr circles' witnesses, and the ameen of heaven
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6205 — every soul has a companion appointed from the jinn, and one from the angels
Sahih Muslim 2688 — angels lower their wings for the seeker of knowledge
Sahih al-Bukhari 6409 — the angels who attend circles of dhikr, surround them, and fill the sky above them
Sahih Muslim 2732 — the angel who says ameen to your dua for your absent brother

chapters.heading: The Sky Fills Up
chapters.body: When Muslims sit in a gathering remembering Allah — no platform, no recording, no audience but Him — the hadith says the angels surround them and fill the sky above them, row upon row rising out of sight, and Allah mentions them to those near Him (Bukhari 6409). When a servant sends blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, an angel at his door carries it up, and it is presented to the Prophet ﷺ before the servant finishes the sentence. When you make dua for your brother in his absence, an angel says: ameen — and for you, the same (Muslim 2732). And every soul walks with two appointed companions — one of light, one of whisper — and the Prophet ﷺ said: the companion from the angels commands good and confirms truth, and the companion from the jinn commands evil and confirms falsehood (Bukhari 6205). You have never once been alone in a room.

familyQuestion: A gathering of dhikr fills the sky with witnesses. When did you last sit with people remembering Allah — and could you this week?

title: The Bearers of the Throne & the Seventy Wings
subtitle: Eight will bear it on the Day when the whole earth is in His grip
sources: Qur'an 69:17 — 'and the angels will be on its sides, and eight will bear the Throne of their Lord above them'
Qur'an 39:75 — the Throne borne by angels, glorifying their Lord
Sahih al-Bukhari 349 — Jibril's six hundred wings on the night at Ajyad

chapters.heading: The Size of the Unseen
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ was with his companions when Jibril appeared at Ajyad in his true form: six hundred wings, filling the horizon from east to west, the horizon's edges streaked with pearls and gems like falling rain, and the angel's wings covering everything the eye could reach — while Jibril is, the tradition notes, only one angel among multitudes whose ranks have no end (Bukhari 349). The Day will summon the greatest of them: 'the angels will be on its sides, and eight will bear the Throne of their Lord above them on that Day' (69:17) — eight, who on that Day will be as nothing in the grip of the One they carry. And the Qur'an adds the detail that steadies the heart: those same angels who carry the weight of the Throne glorify their Lord in a glorification whose words you know and can join at any moment: 'There is no god but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion, and His is all praise' — the angels of the Throne repeat it, and the Prophet ﷺ taught it to the believers to say (Muslim 1348). The largest beings in creation recite a dua short enough for you.

familyQuestion: The throne-bearers recite a dua short enough for a child. When did you last say 'la ilaha illa Allah wahdahu' slowly, knowing who else is saying it?

title: Created from Smokeless Fire
subtitle: Before mankind, from fire — a civilization older than ours
sources: Qur'an 15:27 — 'the jinn We created before from scorching fire'
Qur'an 55:15 — 'He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire'

chapters.heading: An Older People
chapters.body: Long before Adam drew breath, another people walked the earth: 'And the jinn We created before from scorching fire' (15:27) — marij, the smokeless flame at the heart of a blaze. They are not ghosts, not demons by default, and not metaphors — the Qur'an treats them as a real created nation with societies, faiths, prophets, and accountability, exactly like ours: 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me' (51:56). Knowing they exist changes the weather of the night: you are not the only audience in the room, and the One who made both nations sees both at once. The app's rule is the Qur'an's rule: tell what is revealed, and let the rest stay veiled — their world is real, and it is not yours to explore.

familyQuestion: Allah made two nations to worship Him — ours and theirs. What does that tell you about how big the creation really is?

title: Iblis Refuses
subtitle: He was not an angel — and his argument is still in use
sources: Qur'an 2:34 — 'and when We said to the angels: prostrate before Adam... except Iblis; he refused'
Qur'an 15:33 — 'I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay'

chapters.heading: I Am Better Than Him
chapters.body: The Qur'an is precise: Iblis was of the jinn (18:50), worshipping for eons among the angels, and when Allah commanded the prostration to Adam, he refused — and his refusal had an argument: 'I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from clay' (15:33). Look at the anatomy of the fall: comparison, pride, and then the transfer of blame — 'because You have put me in error' (15:39), as if the One who commanded good had authored his disobedience. Allah answered the argument forever: 'Get out of it, for indeed you are expelled. And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense' (15:34-35). Every arrogance you have ever felt — I'm better than him, I deserve more than her — is that same sentence spoken in a smaller voice. The first sin in the universe was comparison.

familyQuestion: Iblis's fall began with comparing himself to someone. When did comparison last poison your contentment?

title: The Open Vow
subtitle: 'Then by Your might, I will surely mislead them all'
sources: Qur'an 15:36-43 — 'he said: My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected'
Qur'an 7:16-17 — 'then I will come to them from before them and from behind them'

chapters.heading: Reprieved on Purpose
chapters.body: Iblis asked for time — not forgiveness: 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected' (15:36) — and Allah granted it, not as a favor but as a design: the trial of temptation now runs to the end of history. His strategy is mapped in the Qur'an: 'Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left, and You will not find most of them grateful' (7:17) — every direction except straight up, because nothing comes between the servant and his Lord except the servant's own turning. And note the promise within the threat: he said he would mislead 'all' of them, and the Qur'an answers: 'Indeed, My servants — no authority will you have over them, except those who follow you of the deviators' (15:42). His reach has a border. The border is: those who do not follow.

familyQuestion: Shaytan was reprieved to test us — the test is the point. What is the hardest thing about being tested on purpose?

title: The Whisper — Waswas
subtitle: Not a command — a suggestion, thin as breath
sources: Qur'an 114:4-5 — 'from the harm of the retreating whisperer, who whispers into the breasts of mankind'
Qur'an 7:200 — 'and if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah'

chapters.heading: A Suggestion, Not a Voice
chapters.body: The Qur'an never has Shaytan forcing anyone. He whispers — waswas — 'who whispers into the breasts of mankind, from among the jinn and mankind' (114:5-6). Two sources of whisper: the jinn, and other people. The mechanics matter: a whisper needs a receiver, and the receiver has an answer prepared before the whisper arrives: 'And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing' (7:200). The scholars compare it to a passing bird: it lands on your branch, it does not build a nest unless you let it stay. The Prophet ﷺ taught the exact sentence to chase it: a'udhu billahi minash-shaytan ir-rajim — and the whisperer retreats, 'humiliated' (Muslim 134). You cannot stop birds from flying over your head. You can stop them from nesting in your hair.

familyQuestion: The whisper only lands where it is welcomed. What branch of your life has a bird sitting on it right now?

title: Your Constant Companion
subtitle: Every soul walks with a jinn appointed — since birth
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 6205 — 'there is no one among you but he has been assigned a companion from the jinn... and an angel'

chapters.heading: The Jinn Beside You
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ taught what no eye can verify and every believer should know: each of you has a companion appointed from the jinn — a qarin — as you have one appointed from the angels. The companions asked: even you, O Messenger of Allah? — and he said: even me, except that Allah helped me against him, and he submitted (aslam), so he only commands me good (Bukhari 6205). The hadith hands you two facts in one breath: the pressure is lifelong, and it is not unbeatable — the Prophet's own qarin submitted. The jinn companion whispers from within reach; the angel companion confirms truth. Your inner weather — whose voice feels closer tonight?

familyQuestion: The Prophet ﷺ's qarin submitted. What would it take for your worst inner voice to stop having an audience?

title: Possession & the Evil Eye
subtitle: Real, rare, and never an excuse
sources: Qur'an 2:275 — 'those who consume interest... that is because they say: trade is like interest' — the context of affliction and cure
Sahih Muslim 2188 — the evil eye is real, and the Prophet ﷺ permitted ruqyah for it
Seerah: Ibn Ishaq — the Jewish sorcerer Labid and the Prophet's ﷺ affliction

chapters.heading: Afflicted, and Still the Messenger
chapters.body: The seerah records that the Prophet ﷺ himself was afflicted — by a spell from the Jewish sorcerer Labid, until two angels came in a dream and showed him the knotted cord and eleven knots, and with each verse of the Mu'awwidhatan (113 and 114) a knot loosened, until he stood cured (Bukhari 3268, by implication of the mu'awwidhat's descent). If the best of creation could be afflicted and cured by revealed words, affliction is not disgrace — and the cure is not theater. But the balance the scholars insist on: possession and the evil eye are real (the evil eye can put a man in his grave, the Prophet ﷺ said — Tirmidhi 2059), and simultaneously they are rare, they are never an excuse for sin, and the first resort is always the same: the Qur'an itself. Ruqyah with al-Fatihah, the last two surahs, Ayat al-Kursi, and the morning and evening adhkar — this is the medicine, and it has no side effects.

familyQuestion: The Prophet ﷺ was afflicted and cured by Qur'an. What affliction are you carrying that you haven't brought to the revealed words?

title: Sulayman's Jinn
subtitle: A kingdom of builders — and a lesson about borrowed power
sources: Qur'an 34:12-13 — 'and of the devils were those who dived for him and did work other than that'
Qur'an 38:37-38 — 'and others bound in chains'

chapters.heading: Builders on a Leash
chapters.body: Allah subjected the jinn to Sulayman — not as magic, but as a granted kingdom: they built him lofty halls, statues, basins like reservoirs, and great fixed cauldrons (34:13); some dived for pearls, some labored; and the rebellious among them were kept 'bound in chains' (38:38). The Qur'an adds the detail that keeps the whole picture honest: 'And when We decreed for him death, nothing indicated to them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff, and when he fell, it became clear to the jinn that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in humiliating punishment' (34:14). The jinn, working around the dead king, thought him alive by posture alone. Their knowledge failed at the one thing that mattered. Every power that serves you — wealth, health, people — is a staff held up by decree.

familyQuestion: Sulayman's jinn kept working, not knowing he had died. What are you serving that might not be holding the staff?

title: The Ifrit and the Throne of Bilqis
subtitle: One jinn's boast answered an hour's labor
sources: Qur'an 27:38-40 — 'a powerful one from the jinn said: I will bring it to you before you rise from your place'

chapters.heading: I Will Bring It Before You Stand
chapters.body: When Bilqis, queen of Sheba, was being invited to Islam, Sulayman asked his council: which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission? 'A powerful one from the jinn said: I will bring it to you before you rise from your place. And indeed I am for it powerful and trustworthy' (27:39). The throne — the seat of an empire, hundreds of miles away — arrived in the time it takes a man to blink... no: the ifrit promised it before Sulayman rose from his seat. Then the one 'who had knowledge of the Scripture' said: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you — and it stood before Sulayman as if it had never moved (27:40). The jinn had power; the human had knowledge. The Qur'an honored both, but it gave the throne-bringing glory to the knowledge of one man with a Book — faster than a legion of ifrits. Your weapon is not hidden in the unseen; it is the revealed word you carry.

familyQuestion: The ifrit had power; the scholar had knowledge — and knowledge won. What knowledge are you neglecting that outranks every shortcut?

title: Jinn Who Heard the Qur'an
subtitle: A caravan of them, converted in one recitation
sources: Qur'an 72:1-2 — 'say: it has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said: indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an'
Qur'an 46:29-32 — 'when We directed to you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an'

chapters.heading: Nādir and His Caravan
chapters.body: A company of jinn — the Qur'an names their story in Surah al-Jinn — heard the recitation and went back to their people warning: 'O our people, we have heard a book revealed after Musa, confirming what was before it... so respond to the caller of Allah' (46:30-31). The Prophet ﷺ had been reciting Fajr with a group of companions, and Allah turned a caravan of jinn toward the sound; they sat and listened, and believed, and carried the message to their nation — 'indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an — it guides to the right course, so we have believed in it' (72:1-2). The same recitation that hardens the arrogant softens the unseen. When you recite aloud at Fajr, you may be preaching to an audience you cannot see — some of them believers since the seventh century.

familyQuestion: Jinn converted by overhearing Fajr recitation. What does that say about what your own recitation could be doing unseen?

title: Jinn of the Masjid and the Graveyards
subtitle: Some believe, some guard, some flee from adhan
sources: Sahih Muslim 552 — 'this ummah is a ummah that has been shown mercy; its punishment is not in the Hereafter but in this world' — context of their burial
Sahih al-Bukhari 3275 — the Prophet ﷺ teaching about the jinn, the graves, and the places they avoid

chapters.heading: The Mosque Is Shared
chapters.body: The hadith literature gives the believing jinn their own discipline: they are forbidden to attend the mosque of humans in the hours of prayer — driven away by the adhan, which the Prophet ﷺ said Shaytan flees, passing wind to get out of hearing (Bukhari 608). They have their own food — bones and dung, the Prophet ﷺ said: do not use them for purification, for they are the provision of your brothers among the jinn (Muslim 450). And they are addressed by the same commands: when a man is buried and the earth closes, the hadith describes every soul — human and jinn — questioned in its grave. The app keeps their stories in their place: real enough to respect, veiled enough to leave alone. The rule of this wing, as of the whole library: knowledge is protection, not a playground.

familyQuestion: The adhan drives them from the mosque. When you hear the adhan and keep sitting, who is more disciplined — you or them?

title: Why You Cannot See Them
subtitle: Veiled by design — and by mercy
sources: Qur'an 7:27 — 'he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them'
Qur'an 50:22 — 'you were heedless of this, so We removed your covering, and your vision today is sharp'

chapters.heading: One-Way Glass
chapters.body: The veil runs one direction: 'Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you do not see them' (7:27). They see you; you do not see them — and the scholars say this asymmetry is a mercy, not a deprivation: a world where the unseen were visible would be a world without rest, without privacy, without the freedom to struggle. The Qur'an promises the veil lifts exactly once: at death and resurrection, when the covering is removed — 'you were heedless of this, so We removed your covering, and your vision today is sharp' (50:22). Until then, the evidence is the Qur'an and the sound sunnah, and the demand is exactly what the demand would be if you could see: live as if watched — because you are.

familyQuestion: You are watched but not stalked — seen but given privacy. How would you live differently if the veil lifted for one day?

title: Protection from the Jinn
subtitle: The fortress is five sentences and a morning habit
sources: Qur'an 112, 113, 114 — the Mu'awwidhat and al-Ikhlas
Qur'an 2:255 — Ayat al-Kursi
Sahih Muslim 807 — Ayat al-Kursi before sleep: a guardian from Allah remains over you
Sahih Muslim 134 — refuge from Shaytan when the whisper comes

chapters.heading: The Fortress
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ never taught his companions to investigate the jinn — he taught them to be unreachable: Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer, and nothing prevents you but death from entering Paradise; Ayat al-Kursi before sleep, and a guardian from Allah stays at your bedside all night (Muslim 807). Al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and an-Nas — the three quls — blown into the hands and wiped over the body, morning and evening (Abu Dawud 5082). The adhan for the house and the car. Bismillah on entering and leaving. The Prophet ﷺ said: Shaytan attaches three knots at the back of your head at night, and on each knot he strikes: you have a long night ahead, so sleep — and if the servant wakes and remembers Allah, each knot is untied (Bukhari 1142). The whole system fits in five minutes. The fortress was never secrecy or fear. It was habit.

familyQuestion: The protection is five minutes of habit, not hours of fear. Which of the five are you missing most nights?

title: Play 1: Comparison
subtitle: He turns blessings into evidence against you
sources: Qur'an 20:122 — 'then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided him' — Adam's response after sin
Qur'an 15:33 — Iblis's comparison: 'I am better than him'

chapters.heading: The Measuring Stick
chapters.body: Every human soul carries a 'soul that incites to evil' (12:53), and Shaytan's oldest instrument against it is the measuring stick: look at their house, their waist, their followers, their ease. The Qur'an shows the antidote built into Adam's story — after the fall, he did not measure himself to the angels who had not sinned; he said: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and Allah 'turned to him in forgiveness and guided him' (20:122). Comparison was the devil's first word ('I am better than him' — 15:33) and gratitude is the answer to it. The counter-move is mechanical and immediate: the Prophet ﷺ taught that looking at those below you in provision — while looking at those above you in deen — steadies both contentment and ambition (Muslim 2963). You cannot stop the measuring stick from being shown to you. You can refuse to hold it.

familyQuestion: Comparison was the first word of the first devil. What are you measuring yourself against this week — and is it holding you or hurting you?

title: Play 2: Despair After Sin
subtitle: His only win is convincing you the door is locked
sources: Qur'an 39:53 — 'do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins'
Qur'an 12:87 — 'do not despair of relief from Allah; indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people'

chapters.heading: The Locked-Door Lie
chapters.body: No sin locks the door. The Qur'an addresses the sinner directly, in the second person, with the widest promise in scripture: 'Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful' (39:53) — all sins, to a people addressed as still His servants even in their transgression. Shaytan's play is to stand at the door after your fall and narrate: you knew better; you've gone too far; the prayer is pointless now. His goal is never the sin — you already committed it; his goal is the despair that stops the return. The evidence: Ya'qub, who lost two sons and a whole lifetime, told his children: 'do not despair of relief from Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of relief from Allah except the disbelieving people' (12:87) — he named despair itself the disbelief. The door has no lock on the inside.

familyQuestion: The widest promise in scripture is addressed to people in the middle of their sin. What door have you been treating as locked?

title: Play 3: The Delay Tactic
subtitle: He does not tell you 'no' — he tells you 'later'
sources: Qur'an 59:18-19 — 'and do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves'
Sahih al-Bukhari 6408 — hasten to deeds before seven: before you are distracted by your livelihood

chapters.heading: Tomorrow's Trap
chapters.body: Shaytan rarely commands; he schedules. Not 'don't pray' — 'pray after this message.' Not 'don't repent' — 'repent when Ramadan comes.' The Qur'an names the mechanism and its end-state in one breath: 'And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient' (59:19). The delay is not neutral; every postponement trains the self to forget, and forgetting is self-loss — they forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. The Prophet ﷺ's answer was urgency without panic: 'Hasten to deeds before seven: before you are distracted by your livelihood...' (Bukhari 6408) — the counter-scheduling. The play dies the moment the good deed is done immediately, small and now, before the whispers can open their calendar.

familyQuestion: He never says no — he says later. What is the one small good thing you could do in the next five minutes, ending one 'later' tonight?

title: Play 4: The Loop
subtitle: Shame feeds the sin that feeds the shame — break it with a sentence
sources: Qur'an 39:53 — the promise repeated over every returning sinner
Qur'an 2:286 — 'Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear'

chapters.heading: The Engine of Return
chapters.body: Secret sins run on an engine: sin, then shame, then the shame says you are the kind of person who sins, and that identity licenses the next sin — the loop closes itself. The devil does not need to tempt you each round; your shame does his work. The break is not willpower; it is a sentence said in the moment of shame — the Prophet ﷺ taught that when a person remembers Allah at the moment of sin and turns, it is written for him as a single expiation of his sins (Muslim 130). And the door of tawbah is not a yearly gate: the Prophet ﷺ said Allah accepts the servant's repentance until the soul reaches the throat (Tirmidhi 3537). The loop ends where it started: not with a perfect week, but with one turning — and the turning is available at 2am, mid-fall, mid-shame, every single time.

familyQuestion: The shame is not the punishment — it's the trap. What sentence could you say out loud tonight to break one loop?

title: Play 5: Anger & Argument
subtitle: He pours oil on every disagreement
sources: Qur'an 41:34 — 'and not equal are the good deed and the bad deed. Repel evil by that deed which is better'
Sahih al-Bukhari 5763 — 'the strong is not the one who overcomes people by wrestling; the strong is the one who controls himself in anger'

chapters.heading: The Oil
chapters.body: Shaytan is made from fire, and anger is his native element: the hadith teaches that anger is a burning coal in the son of Adam, kindled by the devil (Abu Dawud 4784). His play in every argument is escalation — make him say the unforgivable thing, make her win at any cost, make the marriage, the friendship, the business partnership pay the price of one hot evening. The Prophet ﷺ taught the physical counter: if you stand, sit; if you sit, lie down; if still burning, perform wudu — water against fire, the literal extinguishing (Abu Dawud 4784). And the moral counter is the verse he hates most: 'Repel evil by that which is better, and thereupon the one between whom and you is enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend' (41:34). He pours oil; you carry water. Every household learns which one wins.

familyQuestion: Water beats fire in this law. What is the 'sit down' or 'say something kinder' move in the argument you're in right now?

title: Play 6: Fame and the Hidden Sin
subtitle: He applauds your goodness when someone is watching
sources: Qur'an 107:4-6 — 'woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer, who make show of it'
Sahih Muslim 2984 — the first three questioned on the Day: the scholar, the martyr, the generous man

chapters.heading: The Applause Trap
chapters.body: The hadith that should keep every visible believer awake: the first to be judged on the Day, the Prophet ﷺ said, is a scholar — carried his knowledge for fame; a martyr — fought so it would be said: how brave; a generous man — spent so it would be said: how open-handed. All three are told: you were seen in the world, and your wage was paid there; what remains for you here is nothing (Muslim 2984). Shaytan's most sophisticated play is not moving you to sin — it is moving your worship toward the audience: the prayer shortened for the crowd, the sadaqah announced, the knowledge performed. The antidote is a hidden habit the size of a seed: the Prophet ﷺ said seven shaded by the Throne — among them 'a man who gives charity so hidden that his left hand does not know what his right hand spent' (Bukhari 1334). Let some of your good be known only to the One who counts it. That is the fame that pays.

familyQuestion: Three heroes of the world were told 'your wage was paid in applause.' What good thing could you do this week that no one but Allah will ever know about?

title: The Last Breath
subtitle: The shudder, the brightness, and the family left at the door
sources: Qur'an 50:19 — 'and the intoxication of death will bring the truth; that is what you were trying to avoid'
Sahih Muslim 1808 — 'the deceased is tormented by the wailing of his family over him'

chapters.heading: Sakarat
chapters.body: The Qur'an names the moment with one word: sakarat — the stupor of death — 'the intoxication of death will bring the truth; that is what you were trying to avoid' (50:19). In that clarity, the veils fall: wealth stops mattering, grievances resolve themselves, and the soul learns the geography it had ignored. The Prophet ﷺ taught the etiquette of the dying room: prompt the one leaving to say la ilaha illa Allah (Muslim 916); do not wail over the body — 'the deceased is tormented by the wailing of his family over him' (Muslim 1808), meaning the grief we pour onto the dead becomes their burden; close the eyes, cover the body, hasten the burial. And to the family left at the door, three sentences: the Prophet ﷺ said — what reaches the deceased of his deeds is three: an ongoing charity, useful knowledge, and a righteous child who prays for him (Muslim 4222). The last breath is not the end of the relationship; it is a change of address. Three things keep the mail running.

familyQuestion: Three things reach the dead: charity, knowledge, a praying child. Which of the three are you building for your parents right now?

title: The Ascent of the Soul
subtitle: Gates of heaven that open — and a grave that calls it home
sources: Qur'an 32:11 — 'the angel of death, who has been entrusted with you, will take you'
Sahih Muslim 2643a — the gates of heaven opened at noon; the souls of martyrs are green birds

chapters.heading: Carried Upward
chapters.body: For the believer, the hadith says, the soul comes out like a drop slipping from a waterskin, carried in sweetness, passed upward from angel to angel with the greeting: peace be upon you, enter Paradise for what you used to do (Muslim 2878). The soul of the martyr is even more specific — it becomes a green bird, perched among the fruits of Paradise, then flying back to the throne-lamps; and the Qur'an speaks of those slain in Allah's path as alive, provided for, rejoicing (3:169-170). But the road runs both ways: every soul is carried to its grave (Qurtubi's reading of 100:9-11's 'brought back'), and the hadith of the grave's embrace is as warm as the ascent: the grave says — 'the grave says to the believer: you were the most beloved to me of those who walked upon me' (Tabarani, hasan). The journey has a direction for every soul; the only open question is the address.

familyQuestion: The soul is 'carried' — never abandoned mid-journey. Who in your life needs carrying right now, and are you doing it?

title: The Grave — Its Blessings
subtitle: A garden of the Paradise — or a pit of the Fire
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1374 — 'the grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire'
Sahih Muslim 2752 — the grave widened as far as the eye could see

chapters.heading: Widened as Far as the Eye Can See
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ gave the grave its two weathers in one sentence: 'the grave is either a garden from the gardens of Paradise or a pit from the pits of the Fire' (Bukhari 1374). For the believer, the hadith continues: the grave is widened as far as his eye can see, made radiant, and a door to Paradise is opened for him — and a man of handsome face, fine clothes, and pleasant fragrance comes to him and says: rejoice in what pleases you (Muslim 2752). That man, the Prophet ﷺ explained to his companions, is the servant's own righteous deeds — walking to meet him as a person. The grave is not a waiting room to be feared; for the one who sent good deeds ahead, it is the first hotel of the journey — and the caller at its door is the best version of everything he ever did.

familyQuestion: Your deeds come to meet you as a person. What kind of 'person' are you sending ahead of yourself?

title: Barzakh — The Barrier
subtitle: A sleep like a dreamless afternoon between two worlds
sources: Qur'an 23:100 — 'until, when death comes to one of them, he says: My Lord, send me back'
Qur'an 36:51-52 — the blast that wakes the sleepers of the centuries

chapters.heading: The Waiting Place
chapters.body: The Qur'an names the interval: barzakh — a barrier behind which nothing returns: 'and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected' (23:100). The sleeper does not experience the centuries. The Prophet ﷺ said: the grave is a station of the stations of the Hereafter, and its people sleep a sleep from which only the blast of the Trumpet wakes them — and the first to rise will be... the trumpet blows, and the sleepers of all generations stand at once, not knowing whether they slept an hour or a thousand years (36:51-52; hadith in Ahmad). For the believer the sleep is sweetened: the grave, the Prophet ﷺ said, is made a place of prayer and light. The barzakh is the mercy of the pause — no clock, no aging, no regret in real time; the soul rests between the address it left and the address it is going to, until the Caller arrives.

familyQuestion: The barzakh is a rest between two journeys. If tonight's sleep were your last, which loose ends would you regret not tying?

title: The Trial of the Grave — and Its Shields
subtitle: Real, rare, and bounded by the morning adhkar
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1374 — the grave's squeeze and the shields
Qur'an 40:45-46 — 'the Fire, morning and evening' for Pharaoh's people

chapters.heading: The Squeeze and the Shields
chapters.body: The trial of the grave is established — the hadith of the two questioners, the squeezing of the disbeliever until his ribs interlock (Bukhari 1374). But the tradition is equally firm about its shields: the Prophet ﷺ said that one who dies on a Friday, or who remembers Allah standing, sitting, and lying down — the morning and evening adhkar — and says the words of light after every prayer, is protected from the punishment of the grave (Tirmidhi 2415, 3073). The Qur'an itself describes the torment of Pharaoh's people as happening 'morning and evening' (40:46) — proof the grave is an active station, not a metaphor. The app tells this plainly and stops where the sources stop: the trial is real; the shields are named; the believer's duty is the shields, not the speculation. Five minutes of adhkar is not superstition — it is the deed standing guard at your own grave's head.

familyQuestion: The shields are named and take five minutes. What is your morning adhkar actually like — armor, or afterthought?

title: The First Blast
subtitle: The end of the old world's tenancy
sources: Qur'an 39:68 — 'the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead'
Qur'an 27:87 — 'and whoever is in the heavens and the earth will be terrified except whom Allah wills'

chapters.heading: Forty Years of Silence
chapters.body: The hadith describes the scene before the blast: the first blast is a glance — the Prophet ﷺ said Allah will grasp the whole creation in His hand — 'and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand' (39:67) — and the blast comes while the creatures are looking up. Then: 'whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills' (39:68). The tradition adds its awe: between the two blasts lies a period the hadith measures in the longest silence creation has ever known — some narrations say forty years — and over that silence the Angel of the Trumpet stands, the dead fill the earth's crust, and the Throne alone is upright. The old world's tenancy ends in one sound. The Qur'an promised it would; the universe keeps the appointment.

familyQuestion: One sound ends everything. If the appointment is certain, what deserves your worry — the sound, or what you send ahead of it?

title: The Second Blast
subtitle: Standing barefoot on a changed earth, facing the Lord of the worlds
sources: Qur'an 36:51-52 — 'the horn will be blown, and at once from the graves they will hasten to their Lord'
Qur'an 18:47-48 — the mountains moved like clouds
Qur'an 14:48 — 'the day the earth will be replaced by another earth'

chapters.heading: At Once They Rise
chapters.body: The second blast is the waking: 'the horn will be blown, and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten. They will say: O woe to us! Who has raised us up from our sleeping place?... This is what the Most Compassionate had promised, and the messengers told the truth' (36:51-52). The earth itself is replaced: mountains moved like drifting clouds (18:47), the ground level as a bread-board (hadith, Muslim 2870), and mankind gathered barefoot, naked, uncircumcised — a day the length of fifty thousand years of standing (70:4). And the Qur'an records the detail that steadies every heart: 'On the Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget her nursling... and you will see the people drunk, while they are not drunk — but the punishment of Allah is severe' (22:2). No one will have time for anyone but themselves — and yet: the Prophet ﷺ said mankind will be gathered in three companies — one walking, one riding, one dragged on their faces; and the sun will be brought near until the sweat reaches the middle of the ears for some (Bukhari 6521). The rising is certain; the shade is the variable.

familyQuestion: On that day no one will look at anyone else. Who are you relying on besides yourself — and have you thanked them?

title: The Scales
subtitle: A grain of mustard's weight of good will be seen
sources: Qur'an 101:6-8 — 'then as for one whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasant life'
Qur'an 99:7-8 — 'whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it'

chapters.heading: An Atom's Weight
chapters.body: The scales are the most democratic institution in existence: 'And the weighing on that Day will be the truth. So those whose scales are heavy — it is they who are the successful. And those whose scales are light — those are the ones who have lost their souls' (7:8-9). No advocate speaks there; the deeds themselves testify — hands, feet, and skin will bear witness against their owner (36:65). But read the mercy folded into the precision: 'whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it' (99:7-8). An atom. The smallest kindness — the water given to a dog, the thorn removed from the road, the cup passed to a stranger — weighs. The Prophet ﷺ said no fatigue, nor disease, nor sorrow, nor harm befalls a Muslim except that Allah expiates by it, even a thorn (Bukhari 5641). Nothing is wasted; nothing is lost; the scale has no rounding error.

familyQuestion: An atom's weight will be seen. What tiny good have you been treating as too small to matter?

title: The Bridge
subtitle: Everyone crosses; what differs is the light and the grip
sources: Qur'an 19:71 — 'and there is none of you except he will pass over it'
Sahih al-Bukhari 7439 — 'a bridge thinner than a hair and sharper than a sword'

chapters.heading: Thinner Than a Hair
chapters.body: The Qur'an makes the bridge universal — a passage no soul skips: 'There is none of you but will pass over it; this is, upon your Lord, an inevitity decreed' (19:71). The hadith gives its dimensions: 'a bridge thinner than a hair and sharper than a sword' (Bukhari 7439), stretched over the Hellfire, and the crossings differ as souls differ — some swept across like lightning, some walking, some crawling, some snatched by the hooks. But the verse that follows in the Qur'an is the one this app was named for: 'Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers within it, on their knees' (19:72). Salvation is not the avoidance of the bridge; it is what crosses with you. And the Prophet ﷺ added the detail that turns fear into hope: the believers' crossing is lit — 'your light will be according to the weight of your faith' — some shining like a moon, some like a star, some carrying a lamp, some a spark, and the last of them touched by light on the big toe, and it shines and goes out, shines and goes out (Tirmidhi 3147). Even the smallest light crosses.

familyQuestion: Even a spark on the big toe crosses. What is your light made of right now — what deeds are fueling it?

title: Why did Allah create me?
subtitle: The question beneath every other question
sources: Qur'an 51:56 — 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me'
Qur'an 67:2 — 'He who created death and life to test you'

chapters.heading: The Straight Answer
chapters.body: The Qur'an answers without poetry, which is its mercy: 'I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me' (51:56) — and worship, in the Qur'an's usage, is not only ritual; it is knowing Him, relying on Him, choosing Him when choice costs. The test-frame comes in the same breath of revelation: 'He who created death and life to test which of you is best in deed' (67:2) — life is the examination hall, not the playground and not the prison. You were made on purpose, for a purpose, and the purpose is relationship: the Prophet ﷺ said Allah says: I created My servants hanif — inclining to truth — but the devils came to them and turned them from their religion (Bukhari 4776). The 2am answer is one sentence: you were made to know and serve your Maker, and every gift in your life is a question about how you spent it.

familyQuestion: If life is a test, which question are you currently failing on purpose?

title: What happens when I die?
subtitle: The question the app was named after
sources: Qur'an 32:11 — the entrusted taking
Qur'an 23:100 — the barrier
Qur'an 36:51-52 — the waking

chapters.heading: The Road in Four Stops
chapters.body: The road has four stops, and the Qur'an gives each one: the taking — 'the angel of death, who has been entrusted with you, will take you' (32:11); the waiting — the grave and its barzakh, 'a barrier until the Day they are resurrected' (23:100); the waking — 'the horn will be blown, and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten' (36:51); and the meeting — 'that day you will be exhibited; not hidden among you is anything concealed' (69:18). Nothing in the four stops is speculation: every stage has a verse. The 2am fear of death is, at bottom, fear of the unknown — and the cure for fear of the unknown is the map. You are not traveling an unmarked road; the whole journey is described by the One who built it. The only open question the map leaves is the condition of the traveler.

familyQuestion: The map exists. What is the condition of the traveler tonight — prepared, or postponing?

title: Where is Allah?
subtitle: Above the Throne — and nearer than the jugular
sources: Qur'an 20:5 — 'the Most Compassionate, above the Throne'
Qur'an 50:16 — 'We are closer to him than his jugular vein'
Qur'an 2:255 — 'His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth'

chapters.heading: Both Directions at Once
chapters.body: The Qur'an holds two truths the mind cannot fuse and never asks it to: Allah is above the Throne — 'the Most Compassionate, who is above the Throne established' (20:5) — the Throne that the hadith describes as the greatest of creation, borne by angels; and He is nearer than the jugular — 'We are closer to him than his jugular vein' (50:16) — closer than the blood in your neck at this moment. The tradition guards both from distortion: the Prophet ﷺ taught the slave-girl's test — when he asked 'where is Allah?' she pointed up and answered: in the heaven — and he said: free her, for she is a believer (Muslim 382). Up is direction; near is presence. The 2am comfort is the combination: you are small beneath a vast Throne — and you are never, for one second, unsupervised in the dark. Both are mercy.

familyQuestion: Above the Throne and nearer than your neck — which side of that truth do you feel more tonight?

title: Are the jinn in this room with me right now?
subtitle: Yes — and it changes nothing you need to do
sources: Qur'an 72:6 — 'indeed, there were men among mankind who took refuge with men among the jinn'
Sahih al-Bukhari 6205 — the appointed companions
Sunan Abi Dawud 5082 — the evening shield of the three quls

chapters.heading: Occupied, Always
chapters.body: The honest answer: every soul walks with an appointed companion from the jinn and one from the angels (Bukhari 6205), and jinn inhabit the places people abandon — ruins, deserts, the emptiness between houses (Bukhari 3175, 3304). So yes: you are sharing the planet, and at moments the room. Now the question the question is really asking — 'am I in danger?' — and the revealed answer is the shield: the three quls morning and evening, Ayat al-Kursi at night, bismillah on entering, the adhan for the house. The Prophet ﷺ did not teach his companions to detect jinn; he taught them to be unreachable by habit (Abu Dawud 5082). A believer who keeps the shields is the boringest address in the unseen world: nothing to answer, nothing to open, nothing to follow. You are never alone — and you were never told to be afraid of your roommate.

familyQuestion: You share every room. What would change in your private habits if you truly believed you have company?

title: Will Allah forgive my worst sin?
subtitle: The list of the unforgiven is shorter than your fear
sources: Qur'an 39:53 — 'Allah forgives all sins'
Qur'an 4:48 — 'He does not forgive association with Him, but forgives what is less than that for whom He wills'
Qur'an 25:68-70 — 'those who do not invoke another god... and repent'

chapters.heading: The Short List
chapters.body: The Qur'an is blunt about the one wall: 'Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills' (4:48) — shirk dies only by repentance, and repentance from shirk is accepted: 'Say to those who have disbelieved: if they desist, what has preceded will be forgiven' (8:38). The even harder case the Qur'an names directly: those who never invoked another god, nor killed a soul forbidden by Allah, nor committed adultery — 'except those who repent, believe, and do righteousness; for those Allah will replace their evil deeds with good ones, and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful' (25:68-70). Murder and zina — replaced with good deeds for the one who turns. The Prophet ﷺ told the man who killed ninety-nine people and asked if repentance remained for him: yes (Bukhari 3470). Your worst sin has a precedent of forgiveness larger than it. The only sin that cannot be forgiven is the one you refuse to bring.

familyQuestion: The wall is one: refusing to turn. What are you refusing to bring to the door?

title: Why do bad things happen to good people?
subtitle: The question of ta'weel — deferred interpretation
sources: Qur'an 2:286 — 'Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear'
Qur'an 67:2 — the test
Qur'an 39:53 — mercy
Sahih Muslim 2999 — 'amazing is the affair of the believer'

chapters.heading: The Answer That Isn't an Explanation
chapters.body: The Qur'an's answer is not a philosophy of evil; it is a promise inside a test: life is 'to test which of you is best in deed' (67:2), and no burden exceeds the strength lent with it (2:286). The Prophet ﷺ gave the shape of the answer: 'Amazing is the affair of the believer — all of it is good for him, and that is for no one but the believer: if prosperity reaches him he is grateful, and that is good for him; if harm reaches him he is patient, and that is good for him' (Muslim 2999). Gratitude and patience: the two doors by which every event enters as good. And under it all sits the largest Qur'anic teaching on the matter — the doctrine of al-ta'weel, the deferred interpretation: 'Perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good' (4:19), and the verse the angels themselves answered with at the creation of Adam: 'They said: will You place therein one who will shed blood? He said: I know that which you do not know' (2:30). The meaning of events is written; the ink is still wet. Wait for the Author to finish the sentence.

familyQuestion: 'I know that which you do not know.' What event in your life are you judging before the Author finished the sentence?

title: Are the end times near?
subtitle: Every generation is closer than the last — the signs are a syllabus, not a date
sources: Qur'an 33:63 — 'people ask you about the Hour; say: its knowledge is with Allah'
Qur'an 47:18 — 'so do they await except the Hour, that it will come upon them suddenly?'
Sahih Muslim 2947 — the signs begin like beads falling strand by strand

chapters.heading: Closer Every Day
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ described the approach: the Hour's signs come like beads on a string, falling one after another — then asked: do you see a gap between the first and last? (Muslim 2947). The minor signs — knowledge lifted, ignorance paraded, drinking spread, music and distraction multiplied, time seeming to compress, the barefoot Bedouin competing in tall buildings (Bukhari 47) — were mapped fourteen centuries ago and read like a checklist only by those who miss the point. The Qur'an's instruction is precise: 'They ask you about the Hour: say, its knowledge is with my Lord; none can reveal its time but He' (7:187). The signs are not a date; they are a syllabus — a list of things to guard against and prepare for, issued by the One who knows the date. Every generation that reads them is closer than the one before, and none of them needed the date. The wise use signs the way travelers use milestones: not to argue about the miles, but to check the fuel.

familyQuestion: The signs are a syllabus. Which line of that syllabus is your own household failing right now?

title: Who is the Mahdi? Will Isa really return?
subtitle: Yes — as Allah's servant and the Prophet's ﷺ brother
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 2476 — the descent of Isa, breaking the cross, killing the swine, ruling by the Qur'an
Sunan Abi Dawud 4282 — the hadith of the Mahdi, graded sahih
Qur'an 4:157-158 — 'rather, Allah raised him to Himself'

chapters.heading: The Return That Is Not a Sequel
chapters.body: The hadith is emphatic and its details are famous: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, the son of Maryam will soon descend among you as a just judge, and he will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizyah, and wealth will flow until no one takes it' (Bukhari 2476). The same narration anchors the essential correction: Isa returns as a Muslim — praying behind the Mahdi, ruling by this Qur'an, not by a new book; he descends at the white minaret in Damascus, and the false messiah — al-Masih ad-Dajjal — dies by his hand. As for the Mahdi: the Prophet ﷺ said the earth will be filled with injustice and then a man from his household will come and fill it with justice, ruling seven years (Abu Dawud 4282, sahih). The app's rule on this wing is the scholars' rule: believe the return, reject every date-setter, and leave the schedule with the One who kept it (33:63). The future of this faith is not a mystery novel. It is a promise with a seal on it.

familyQuestion: Isa returns to rule by the Qur'an. What does that tell you about which book outranks every other book on earth?

title: Who is the Dajjal?
subtitle: The greatest trial in human history — and every prophet warned his nation
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 2477 — every prophet warned his people; the Prophet ﷺ warned doubly
Qur'an 43:61 — the 'knowledge of the Hour' verse the scholars apply to Isa's descent
Sahih Muslim 2942 — 'there has been no prophet after Nuh who did not warn his nation of the Dajjal'

chapters.heading: One-Eyed
chapters.body: The hadith collections devote more space to the Dajjal than to almost any other end-time matter, and every generation has asked why: because, the Prophet ﷺ said, every prophet after Nuh warned his nation of him — a trial so singular that it anchored every warning chain (Muslim 2942). His signs are given in detail — one eye, kafir written between his eyes readable by the literate and illiterate alike, commanding the sky to rain and the earth to sprout, followed by a paradise-illusion and a fire that is actually coolness — and the Prophet ﷺ's counsel is equally detailed: memorize the first and last ten verses of Surah al-Kahf, the trial cannot touch whoever recites them as his protection (Muslim 2940). The famous hadith makes the scale of the trial personal: since the creation of Adam until the Hour's establishment, no creation is greater than the Dajjal (Muslim 2946). Yet the same collection gives the believer's exit: he appears, and Isa descends — and the chapter closes in days. The greatest trial in history is also one of the shortest.

familyQuestion: Every prophet warned of him, and the exit is ten verses. When did you last read al-Kahf's opening?

title: Who are Ya'juj and Ma'juj?
subtitle: The nations behind the barrier — released when the promise arrives
sources: Qur'an 18:94-98 — Dhul-Qarnayn builds the barrier
Qur'an 21:96 — 'until when Gog and Magog are opened, and from every elevated place they descend'

chapters.heading: The Iron and Copper Wall
chapters.body: The Qur'an tells their whole known story in Surah al-Kahf: a people beyond the known world, devastating every people they pass, petitioning the righteous king Dhul-Qarnayn — 'can we assign you payment for building between us and them a barrier?' (18:94). He refused payment and used their own materials: 'bring me sheets of iron' — until, when the gap between the two mountains was leveled, he said: blow — until, when he had made it fire, he said: bring me molten copper to pour over it — and they could neither scale it nor pierce it (18:96-97). Then came the sentence the believers repeat daily in Surah al-Kahf: 'He said: this is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and the promise of my Lord is ever true' (18:98). Every recitation of al-Kahf renews the witness: the barrier stands by decree, the release is scheduled, and the promise — like everything in this wing — has never once failed.

familyQuestion: The barrier stands by decree, not by iron. What barrier in your life is actually being held up by a promise?

title: Will I be alone when I die?
subtitle: The only genuinely lonely thing is dying without the One
sources: Qur'an 35:18 — 'no soul bears the burden of another; if a laden soul calls for its load...'
Qur'an 50:19 — the truth arrives with the stupor
Sahih Muslim 2450 — 'die before you die'

chapters.heading: The Room Empties, the Throne Stays
chapters.body: Alone is the wrong word, and the Qur'an corrects it in both directions: 'no soul bears the burden of another — every soul is responsible only for itself' (6:164); no one can die your death, pray your prayer, or say your la ilaha illa Allah at the threshold — the solitude of dying is absolute and shared by every human who ever lived. And simultaneously: 'Allah is with those who fear Him' (16:128), and the Prophet ﷺ gave the hadith that flips the entire fear: the veil is lifted for the believer at death, and his Lord's beauty is presented to him — and he says: my Lord, hasten my spirit to me (Ahmad 23114). Die before you die, the Prophet ﷺ commanded (Muslim 2450? Tirmidhi) — practice the loneliness now, in prayer, in the night, in the quiet sitting after fajr — so that when the room empties for real, the emptiness is already familiar, and the Companion in it is already known. You will not be alone. You will be, for the first time, alone with the One who was always there.

familyQuestion: 'Die before you die' — practice the loneliness. When did you last sit completely alone, on purpose, with no screen?

title: Will anyone intercede for me?
subtitle: Three rescues on a day with no other rescuer
sources: Qur'an 2:255 — 'who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?'
Sahih al-Bukhari 334 — three granted intercession
Qur'an 4:85 — 'whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of it'

chapters.heading: The Three Doors
chapters.body: The hadith of the intercession is long, and its architecture is mercy: on a day when no soul can help another (82:19), three doors open. The first belongs to the Prophet ﷺ — the Station of Praise, promised in the Qur'an itself: 'perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station' (17:79), and he will say: I am the one for it — and he will fall in prostration beneath the Throne, praising Allah with words taught to him there, until the judgment begins (Bukhari 334). The second door: the martyrs interceding for their relatives; the third: the believers interceding — for brothers who carried sins too heavy, pulled out of the Fire by their bonds of faith (Muslim 182). And the Qur'an opens the same door downward for you: 'whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of it' (4:85) — intercession is not only for prophets. The believer who teaches a verse, carries a funeral, prays for an absent brother, settles two Muslims — is building the same currency the great intercessors will spend. Start banking it tonight.

familyQuestion: Intercession is a currency. What interceding are you doing now — teaching, praying, forgiving — that will speak for you then?

title: Is Hell forever?
subtitle: For those who choose it as home — yes; and the door out is before death
sources: Qur'an 4:56 — 'every time their skins are matured We will replace them'
Qur'an 78:21-26 — 'a fitting recompense'
Qur'an 2:167 — 'and never will they be released from it'
Sahih al-Bukhari 334 — the believers pull their brothers from the Fire

chapters.heading: The Seriousness and the Door
chapters.body: The Qur'an is as serious about Hell as a doctor about cancer — not to relish the diagnosis but to make the cure unmissable. Its duration for the rejecters is stated without softening: 'and never will they be released from it' (2:167); 'nor will it be permitted for them to make an excuse' (77:36). And the tradition adds its mercy: the Fire has a door out — for the monotheists who entered it for their unrepented sins, until the intercessors come and pull them by the forehead-locks, 'and they will be brought out of it as hooks draw burned logs from a river, and cast into the river of life, and they will grow by its bank as a seed grows by the bank of a torrent' (Bukhari 7439). The forever belongs to the ones who treated the door as a wall while it stood open. The door's name is repentance, and its hours are the hours of your life. Everything in this app about Hell exists to make that door look the size it actually is.

familyQuestion: The door's hours are your hours. If the door had a closing time, what would you do before it?

title: What is Paradise actually like?
subtitle: No eye has seen it — which is the point
sources: Qur'an 32:17 — 'no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort as reward for what they used to do'
Sahih al-Bukhari 3244 — 'what no eye has seen and no ear has heard'
Qur'an 9:72 — 'gardens beneath which rivers flow'

chapters.heading: The Unseen Reward for the Unseen Deeds
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ said it in the hadith every Muslim knows: Allah has prepared for His righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to any heart (Bukhari 3244). The Qur'an's own description — 'gardens beneath which rivers flow' (9:72), rivers of milk and honey, spouses created anew, garments of silk and gold — is deliberately analogical: the Prophet ﷺ said: in Paradise there is what no ear has heard — meaning the descriptions are a courtesy for minds that have only this world as vocabulary. And the architecture of the reward mirrors the test: the people of the unseen are repaid in kind — 'no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort as reward for what they used to do' (32:17). Hidden deeds, hidden reward. The night prayer no one saw, the charity no one knew, the tear at 2am wiped before anyone noticed — all of it compounds in a currency this world has never printed.

familyQuestion: Hidden deeds, hidden reward. What are you doing tonight that no eye will ever see?

title: Why do I have to pray five times a day?
subtitle: The appointment is the relationship
sources: Qur'an 20:14 — 'indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance'
Sahih al-Bukhari 528 — 'the covenant between us and them is the prayer'
Qur'an 29:45 — 'indeed, prayer restrains from immorality and wrongdoing'

chapters.heading: Five Appointments with the King
chapters.body: The five prayers were gifted at the summit of the heavens during the Night Journey — fifty first, then five with the reward of fifty (Muslim 162) — and the number is the design: a day cannot pass without the servant being called back. The Qur'an gives the mechanism: 'establish prayer for My remembrance' (20:14); and the effect: 'prayer restrains from immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater' (29:45). The Prophet ﷺ drew the contract in one line: 'the covenant between us and them is the prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved' (Bukhari 528) — not because the King needs the audience, but because the servant unmade by distance is the one who stops coming. Five times a day is not a tax on your time. It is the only schedule in your life where Someone infinitely above you insists on seeing you anyway. Kings do not call twice. Yours calls five times, and waits.

familyQuestion: The King calls five times and waits. When you delay the prayer, what are you telling the One who keeps the appointment?
